claims.content: To update and read device rule data in encrypted format to ensure secure system operations.

goal.raw_text: To update and read device rule data in encrypted format to ensure secure system operations.

claims.content: System Administrator
The RLCS application software shall Update and read password and device rule data in encrypted format.
The System Administrator must have a Command Level that permits issuing control commands (i.e., 'Control' or 'Override'), as 'Status Only' users may not issue any control commands.
The System Administrator must be authenticated via the Personnel Security Level entity, which restricts access based on Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.
The System Administrator initiates a request to update device rule data through the RLCS application software.

trigger.raw_text: The System Administrator initiates a request to update device rule data through the RLCS application software.

claims.content: The System Administrator accesses the RLCS application software to update device rule data.
The system verifies that the System Administrator’s Command Level permits issuing control commands (i.e., is not 'Status Only').
The system authenticates the System Administrator using the Personnel Security Level entity, which restricts access based on Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.
The System Administrator inputs or modifies device rule data, including Device Rules ID, Mode, Device X desired status, and Device Y prohibited status.
The RLCS application software updates the device rule data in encrypted format as required by security specifications.
The system stores the updated device rule data in the RLCS database for operational use and historical reporting.
If the System Administrator’s Command Level is 'Status Only', the system shall prevent issuance of any control commands, including device rule updates, and terminate the use case.

If authentication via the Personnel Security Level entity fails (i.e., user lacks required access based on Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, or System Functions), the system shall deny access and exit the use case.
If the RLCS application software cannot update or read device rule data in encrypted format as required, the system shall abort the operation and log a security failure.
The device rule data (Device Rules ID, Mode, Device X desired status, Device Y prohibited status) has been successfully updated in the RLCS database.
The updated device rule data is stored in encrypted format as required by security specifications.
The system retains historical transaction data of the revision for reporting purposes.
The revised rules are now active and will be enforced during subsequent device command operations.
